subject: Post-call: token economics scenarios & region impact
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@finscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: token economics scenarios & region impact

Thanks for the time today, Emily — quick recap and a few asks so we can turn the call into a tight proposal.

Call recap (30 minutes):
- Use case: real-time personalization + analytics (mix of short completions + chat history).
- Traffic split estimate: 50% EU end users, 40% US, 10% APAC (rough).
- Residency requirement: EU customer data must remain in EU for EU end users; backups can be stored in US if encrypted and contractually allowed.

Open asks / requests from our side to finalize pricing scenarios:
1) Expected monthly token range (ballpark): low / typical / peak?
2) Target blended price (your goal $/1M tokens) or budget range for core LLM spend per month?
3) Preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly vs annual commit)?
4) Any hard exclusions for routing/failover (i.e., absolutely no cross-region processing even for fallback)?

Quick hypothesis based on today:
- Initial monthly tokens: 5–10M (you mentioned pilot at ~5M).
- Target price: you said sub-$1k/1M is attractive but we should confirm if $900–$1,200 is realistic for you depending on commit and residency.

I've attached a quick spreadsheet (Redwood_US_EU_quick_econ.xlsx) with simple scenarios (hosted vs dedicated, 0/50/100% EU residency splits) — please confirm the numbers above and add any procurement contact if you'd like us to loop them in.

Next step: after you confirm numbers, we'll deliver a short 1‑pager + a committed pricing strawman and proposed timing for a solutions deep-dive with Marissa (solutions) and our finance lead.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor

Thanks Grace — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token volumes: pilot (Month 1–3) ~5M tokens/mo, growth path to 8–12M tokens/mo by month 6 assuming successful latency tests. Peak bursts could reach ~18M in a week during campaign periods.

2) Target price: our internal goal is < $1,000 / 1M tokens for hosted inference. We can consider a higher blended rate for month 1–3 but want to see committed pricing for months 4+.

3) Residency: EU residency is non-negotiable for EU users — all inference must execute in EU for EU PII/derived profiles. We can allow encrypted backups to US for DR, but only if covered by contract clauses. ~50% of active users are EU right now and that will likely creep up.

4) Billing/cadence: Procurement prefers annual commitments for budgeting, but pilot can be month-to-month with a conversion to an annual commitment if we meet SLOs. Please include both options in the strawman.

Attached is our SOC2 summary we discussed (Finscale_SOC2_summary.pdf). Please send a simple worked example showing how the EU premium affects unit economics (hosted vs dedicated) and the minimum commit needed to hit ~ $900 / 1M.

I'll loop in our procurement lead if we get a strawman that looks reasonable.

Best,

CTO, FinScale

Subject: Re: Post-call: token economics scenarios & region impact — pricing strawman + next steps

Appreciate the clarity, Emily. Attached is a short PDF (high-level-pricing-scenarios.pdf) that walks through three scenarios (pilot hosted, committed hosted, and dedicated reserved). High-level worked example below (all figures approximate; final numbers depend on exact token mix and average seq length):

Worked example (per 1M tokens):
- Hosted (US region): $900 / 1M tokens — assumption: multi-tenant, no residency premium, no commit beyond monthly.
- Hosted (EU region): $1,350 / 1M tokens — +50% regional premium to cover EU infra, data locality, and network egress asymmetry.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, 12m commit @ 10M/mo baseline): US $650 / 1M tokens, EU $950 / 1M tokens.

Notes: the EU delta primarily reflects: (a) higher instance costs in EU zones, (b) additional cross-region replication rules and KMS/HSM provisioning, and (c) smaller regional pool economics for reserved capacity. With a 12-month commit we can usually bring blended EU pricing down ~20–25% relative to hosted month-to-month.

Example: If you land at 8M tokens/mo with 50% EU residency and sign a 12-month dedicated reserve at that baseline, blended $/1M ≈
  ((4M * 650) + (4M * 950)) / 8M = $800 / 1M (very rough).

Proposed next steps:
- 30-minute follow-up: Solutions + Finance deep-dive to validate workloads (we'll bring sample cost model and commit tiers). Marissa, can you join as the solutions lead?
- Suggested slots: Dec 3 10:00–10:30 GMT OR Dec 4 14:00–14:30 CET (we'll convert if those don't work).
- I'll draft a simple two-option strawman (pilot month-to-month; 12m reserved) and share a redlineable SOW.
